messages:
acme_integration: Hey, billing team — we just got a bill that’s ~3x our SDK estimate for March. SDK shows ~4k tokens but invoice shows ~12k. Request id: req_9a1b2c3. Any idea?

olivia (support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal request you sent (curl or SDK) and whether you used streaming or function-calls? Also confirm the exact model.

acme_integration: Sure — we used streaming + function calling. Minimal repro curl below (sanitized):

acme_integration: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-compat-7b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize these logs"}],"functions":[{"name":"log_fetch","parameters":{"type":"object"}}],"stream":true}'
```

acme_integration: SDK (node) call they used to estimate tokens:```js
const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "open-compat-7b",
  messages: [{ role: "system", content: "You are a helpful assistant." },{ role: "user", content: "Summarize these logs" }],
  stream: true,
});
// estimator: client.tokens.estimate(messages) -> 4000 tokens
```

olivia (support): Thanks — two quick asks: 1) could you attach the raw request_id and any X-Redwood headers from the response? 2) Did the assistant trigger a function call and did the tool return a large payload?

acme_integration: Request id: req_9a1b2c3 (same as above). Yes, function call "log_fetch" returned ~6k tokens of log text from our tool service. We assumed estimator counts the function call output the same as assistant output, but numbers don’t match.

ryan (eng-runtime): Heads-up on how metering works: the SDK estimator only tokenizes the messages you pass client-side — it can't account for server-side injected tokens like tool outputs produced after the function-call is executed on the server. Our metering pipeline tokenizes the final conversation after any function/tool messages are inserted and after model post-processing (including separators, role tokens, and any stop/finish markers). That often explains a 1.5-3x delta when tools return large blobs.

ryan (eng-runtime): Also, streaming can cause estimator mismatch: if your estimator measures based on expected completion length but our runtime emits extra metadata tokens or final newline chunks, your client-side estimate will undercount.

olivia (support): @david (billing) can you confirm how invoice counts are computed here?

David (billing): Invoice uses the metering service output (authoritative): we tokenize the final request/response pair as persisted by the runtime. That includes: system messages, user messages, assistant messages, function call messages, and tool outputs inserted as assistant messages. We also include internal separators and special tokens used by the tokenizer (these can add ~1–3% overhead but can be larger for many short fragments). For req_9a1b2c3 our metering log shows tokens=12034.

token-meter-bot: Metering processed req_9a1b2c3 -> tokens=12034, model=open-compat-7b, stage=post-process, pipeline_version=2026-01-12

acme_integration: Ah ok — so the tool output gets counted even though estimator ran before tool ran. Any recommended repro steps so we can validate locally?

ryan (eng-runtime): Repro steps: 1) Send two identical requests: one with stream=true (to mirror your production) and one with stream=false. 2) Ensure the function returns a large payload (>4k chars). 3) Inspect server headers on non-streaming response for X-Token-Count (we emit it for debugging). 4) Compare your estimator result against server header. Example non-streaming curl: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-compat-7b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize these logs"}],"functions":[{"name":"log_fetch","parameters":{} }],"stream":false}' -D -
```

ryan (eng-runtime): If you see a header like `X-Redwood-Token-Count: 12034` that is the authoritative count used for billing. If you need programmatic parity, call our tokenizer endpoint server-side or run the same tokenizer (we can share a small utility) after the function output is attached.

David (billing): For short-term customer relief, if you can provide a list of request_ids and show the estimator output we’ll take a look and consider an adjustment if there’s an obvious mismatch pattern.

acme_integration: Okay — I ran the non-streaming repro and got header `X-Redwood-Token-Count: 11998`. My local estimator still shows ~4000. I’ll paste the raw function output (sanitized) in a DM to Olivia.

olivia (support): Thanks — once we have the function output we’ll escalate to runtime to see if there’s anything unexpected (e.g., duplicate insertion or serialization differences). In parallel, @ryan can you add a short note to the SDK docs about estimator limitations with function/tool outputs and streaming?

ryan (eng-runtime): Will do — I’ll also open an internal ticket to consider returning server-side usage information in-stream for streaming calls so clients can reconcile counts in real time.

acme_integration: Appreciate it. ETA for the internal ticket? We have internal finance folks asking now.

ryan (eng-runtime): I’ll create the ticket today and tag eng-runtime + billing — should have an initial triage within 48 hours. For immediate workarounds: 1) disable streaming for critical billing-sensitive runs, or 2) run the server-side tokenizer after tool output is known.

olivia (support): Closing the loop here: we’ve captured req_9a1b2c3, receipt of your sanitized tool output, and a note for docs + ticket. I’ll follow up with any billing adjustments if we spot anomalies. :thumbsup:

acme_integration: Thanks everyone — that clarifies a lot.
